# SYNTHESISs with `tags` `social-identity`

*Topics — What a work is about. Nucleation holds whatever reading the owner files here, whether or not an Anthology of the SOTA topic could also hold it; instruction for ML practice belongs to the anthology (ADR-048). The words are seeded from the clusters the reading-time triage of 2026-09-25 found, and grow by decision.*

**Social identity** — the psychology of group membership — social identity and self-categorization theory, how people categorize themselves and others and when a group identity becomes salient, identification and its measurement, in-group bias and intergroup relations, rivalry, recategorization and common in-group identity, group-based emotion, crowds and fandom. What a group is, as ontology, is social-ontology; here it is how people come to see themselves and act as members (ADR-062).

| [SYNTHESIS-052](../../../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-052.md) | What a collective is credited with need not be what its members hold: an organized whole's operative intention is not the expectation of its members' intentions and its reasons can part from theirs; a diffuse population with no procedure can show a public stance or change an outside institution without a collective intention, whether the credit is then due to it is open, and composition and a group process are offered as routes by which its most committed or extreme members fix the stance; a person can be organized by a judgement attributed to a collective that does not hold it, governs themselves by making such a judgement's authority depend on its grounds, and that rule holds without qualification only for judgements of what already is; and whether a community of sound inquirers can settle on a belief none of them reasoned to is open, with model results whose tests in real communities are open questions | A part account of the distributed-agency line: the part on what is credited to a collective as against what its members hold. It has three inquiries. The first runs from the owner's thesis that an organized whole's operative intention is not the expectation of its members' ([CLAIM-030](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-030.md)), and its consequence for reasons and polling ([CLAIM-271](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-271.md)), to a population with no procedure at all, credited with a stance or an effect ([QUESTION-119](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-119.md), [CASE-104](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-104.md), [CASE-100](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-100.md)), with A7's distributed cultural uptake ([CLAIM-332](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-332.md)) and two proposed routes by which a minority fixes a fanbase's stance ([CLAIM-490](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-490.md), [CLAIM-493](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-493.md)). The second asks the same question from inside the person credited: a person organized by a judgement attributed to a collective that does not hold it ([CLAIM-415](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-415.md), [TERM-075](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-075.md), [CASE-140](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-140.md) to [CASE-142](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-142.md)), the self-governance that conditions a judgement's authority on its grounds ([CLAIM-425](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-425.md)), and the owner's hyperstition objection ([CLAIM-426](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-426.md)). The third asks whether a community of sound inquirers can settle on a belief none of them reasoned to ([QUESTION-047](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-047.md)), with five questions that hold the real-world tests of its model readings. The line's account is built over it. It adds nothing of its own; its standing is its components'. | Proposed |
